title: Trace consistency through a Neo4j cluster
description: Switch scenarios to see how the routing driver, primary majority, asynchronous secondary, and backup boundary change the user-visible result. Select any component for its responsibility.

nodes.label: Neo4j driver
nodes.detail: Maintains a connection pool and routing table, declares read or write access mode, retries eligible transient failures, and carries bookmarks when causal ordering is required.

nodes.label: Routing table
nodes.detail: Maps the database's current writer, readers, and routers. A routing driver refreshes this view when leadership changes or an address stops accepting the requested mode.

nodes.label: Primary A
nodes.detail: Orders writes for this database and synchronously replicates transaction-log entries to enough primaries for a majority commit.

nodes.label: Primary B
nodes.detail: Acknowledges synchronous replication and can be elected writer when it is sufficiently up to date and receives a majority of votes.

nodes.label: Primary C
nodes.detail: Completes the three-primary fault-tolerance set. With only this copy available, reads may continue but no majority exists for new writes.

nodes.label: Secondary
nodes.detail: Pulls transaction logs asynchronously and serves read-only queries. It can lag and does not vote in the primary commit quorum.

nodes.label: Backup store
nodes.detail: Retains backup artifacts outside the live replication topology. Restore tests prove recovery point, recovery time, constraints, privileges, and application integrity.

scenarios.label: Committed write
scenarios.summary: The driver routes a write transaction to the current writer. The writer synchronously sends the ordered change to the other primaries and completes commit after enough copies confirm a majority.
scenarios.result: In a three-primary topology, the writer plus at least one other primary makes the commit durable against one primary failure.

scenarios.label: Scaled read
scenarios.summary: A read transaction is routed to the asynchronous secondary so analytical or traversal traffic does not consume the writer's capacity.
scenarios.result: Read throughput increases, but a request without a causal bookmark may observe state older than the latest committed write.

scenarios.label: Read own write
scenarios.summary: A write returns a bookmark. The dependent read carries it, so a routed secondary waits until it has applied at least that causal position before executing.
scenarios.result: The user sees the prior write even when the read moves to another copy; the consistency requirement may add replication wait.

scenarios.label: Writer failure
scenarios.summary: The current writer fails. The remaining two primaries still form a majority, elect an up-to-date writer, and cause the routing driver to refresh and retry eligible work.
scenarios.result: Writes pause during detection and election, then resume on Primary B. Application callbacks must remain idempotent because transient work may be retried.

scenarios.label: Majority loss
scenarios.summary: Two of three primaries are unavailable. The surviving primary still has graph state but cannot form a majority to order new writes safely.
scenarios.result: Write transactions are rejected until quorum is restored. Serving stale or read-only traffic is a separate product decision, not automatic write availability.

scenarios.label: Restore proof
scenarios.summary: A backup artifact leaves the live topology and is restored in isolation. Replication health alone cannot prove recovery from deletion, corruption, or operator error.
scenarios.result: A successful restore test records recovered time, data and constraint checks, credentials, application verification, and measured RPO and RTO.
